sentences.text:
For Respondent(s) : Mr. Vikram Rajpurohit, P.P.
 Mr. Vinit Jain, Sr. Adv. assisted by Mr.
 Divakar Sharma, for the complainant  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ARUN MONGA Order(Oral) 10/10/2024 1.

Quashing of FIR No.165/2023 dated 17.05.2023 registered at Police Station Sadar, District Barmer, and all other consequential proceedings emanating therefrom for offences under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 & 120-B of IPC, is sought herein on the basis of compromise arrived between the parties.
2. On a Court query, it transpires that the petitioner (accused) and the complainant are acquainted with each other.
The dispute between the parties pertains to a civil matter involving the land in question, which the petitioner allegedly sold using forged documents.

Due to their personal dispute,
allegations were made against the petitioners in the heat of the moment during the registration of the FIR.

Subsequently, they have buried their hatchet and have entered into a compromise,
pursuant to which, they wish to enjoy their cordiality with each other.
[2024:RJ-JD:41567] (2 of 2) [CRLMP-7051/2024]
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that in view of the compromise between the parties as is borne out from the compromise deed dated 06.10.2024, respondent No.2 - complainant is not inclined to press charges against the petitioner and proceed further in the matter.

sentences.text: He urges that the impugned FIR and all consequential proceedings may be quashed on the basis of compromise.

4. Learned counsel for the respondent No.2-complainant and learned Public Prosecutor concur with the fact of compromise and submit that in view of the compromise, they have no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.

5. In the premise, applying the ratio in decision of Gian Singh (Supra), I deem it just and proper to invoke inherent powers of this Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C (Now Section 528 of BNSS) to avoid undue hardship to the parties for mutual good relations and societal peace.

6. Accordingly, the present misc. petition is allowed and the FIR No.165/2023 dated 17.05.2023 registered at Police Station Sadar, District Barmer, and all other consequential proceedings emanating therefrom for offences under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 & 120-B of IPC, against the petitioner are hereby quashed.
7. Stay petition is also decided accordingly.

(ARUN MONGA),J 191-/Jitender//-
